questions.content:
The table shows the weekly labour market for shop workers in the town of Brandale.

Wage (dollars per hour) | Workers employers want to hire | Workers willing to work
6 | 900 | 300
7 | 800 | 500
8 | 700 | 700
9 | 600 | 900
10 | 500 | 1,100

(a) Identify the equilibrium wage and the number of workers employed at the equilibrium wage. (2 marks)
(b) The government introduces a minimum wage of 9 dollars per hour. Calculate the number of workers who are unemployed at this wage. (1 mark)
(c) Explain one benefit of a minimum wage for workers who keep their jobs. (1 mark)
(d) Explain one way a minimum wage could affect the costs of a business. (1 mark)
questions.mark_scheme:
[1] (a) Equilibrium wage 8 dollars per hour.
[1] (a) Equilibrium employment 700 workers.
[1] (b) 900 - 600 = 300 workers unemployed.
[1] (c) Workers who keep their jobs earn a higher income (9 dollars rather than 8), improving their living standards or reducing poverty.
[1] (d) Wage costs rise, so firms may cut jobs, raise prices or earn lower profits.
Accept other valid points.

questions.content:
The table shows the consumer price index (CPI) for the country of Orrin.

Year | Consumer price index
2022 | 100
2023 | 108
2024 | 114.48

In 2024 the central bank raised the interest rate paid on savings accounts to 5%. Real interest rate = nominal interest rate - inflation rate.

(a) Calculate the rate of inflation in 2023. (1 mark)
(b) Calculate the rate of inflation in 2024. Show your working. (1 mark)
(c) Describe how the inflation rate changed between 2023 and 2024. (1 mark)
(d) Calculate the real interest rate on savings accounts in 2024. (1 mark)
(e) Explain how a rise in interest rates can help to reduce inflation. (2 marks)
questions.mark_scheme:
[1] (a) (108 - 100) / 100 x 100 = 8%.
[1] (b) (114.48 - 108) / 108 x 100 = 6%.
[1] (c) The inflation rate fell from 8% to 6%, but prices are still rising (just more slowly).
[1] (d) 5% - 6% = -1% (savings lose value in real terms).
[1] (e) Higher interest rates make borrowing more expensive and saving more attractive, so households and firms spend and invest less.
[1] (e) Lower total demand reduces pressure on firms to raise prices, so inflation slows.
Accept other valid points.

questions.content:
The town of Kelmoor has three internet providers.

Provider | Customers (thousands)
Nexa | 480
Orbis | 90
Tello | 30

Nexa charges each customer 40 dollars per month. Nexa's average cost of serving one customer is 25 dollars per month. Building a new nationwide network would cost a new firm billions of dollars.

(a) Calculate Nexa's share of the market. (1 mark)
(b) Define the term monopoly. (1 mark)
(c) Calculate Nexa's total monthly profit. Show your working. (2 marks)
(d) Explain one way consumers might be harmed by a firm with a very large market share. (1 mark)
(e) Explain one way consumers might benefit from a firm with a very large market share. (1 mark)
questions.mark_scheme:
[1] (a) 480 / 600 x 100 = 80%.
[1] (b) A market with a single seller (or one firm dominating the market) with barriers that stop other firms entering.
[1] (c) Working: profit per customer (40 - 25 = 15 dollars) x 480,000 customers.
[1] (c) Answer 7.2 million dollars per month (7,200,000).
[1] (d) A valid harm, e.g. higher prices, less choice, lower quality because there is little competition.
[1] (e) A valid benefit, e.g. economies of scale allow lower average costs and lower prices, or large profits fund investment in better networks.
Accept other valid points.

questions.content:
The table shows the government budget of Brevia for one year (billions of dollars).

Revenue | Amount
Income tax | 42
Value added tax (VAT, a tax added to the price of goods and services) | 30
Corporation tax | 18
Other | 10

Spending | Amount
Health | 32
Education | 24
Pensions and welfare | 36
Defence | 8
Other | 12

Use accurate economic terms in your answers.

(a) Calculate the budget balance and state whether it is a deficit or a surplus. (1 mark)
(b) Calculate income tax as a percentage of total government revenue. (1 mark)
(c) Calculate health spending as a percentage of total government spending, to one decimal place. (1 mark)
(d) Distinguish between a direct tax and an indirect tax, using an example of each from the table. (2 marks)
(e) Explain one way the government could reduce its budget deficit. (1 mark)
questions.mark_scheme:
[1] (a) Revenue 100 - spending 112 = -12 billion dollars, a deficit.
[1] (b) 42 / 100 x 100 = 42%.
[1] (c) 32 / 112 x 100 = 28.6%.
[1] (d) Direct tax is paid straight to the government by the person or firm earning the income or profit, e.g. income tax or corporation tax.
[1] (d) Indirect tax is added to the price of goods and services and paid when buying them, e.g. VAT.
[1] (e) A valid method with a brief reason, e.g. raise tax rates to increase revenue, or cut spending on some areas to reduce expenditure.
Accept other valid points.

questions.content:
The country of Orlan imports bicycles. The government is considering a tariff (a tax on imported goods).

Without a tariff: world price of a bicycle = 200 dollars. Domestic firms produce 20,000 bicycles a year and 60,000 are imported.

With a 20% tariff on imported bicycles: the price of a bicycle in Orlan rises to 240 dollars. Domestic firms produce 30,000 bicycles a year and 35,000 are imported.

(a) Calculate the amount of the tariff on each imported bicycle. (1 mark)
(b) Calculate the government's annual revenue from the tariff. Show your working. (2 marks)
(c) Calculate the percentage change in the number of bicycles produced by domestic firms. (1 mark)
(d) Explain one way that consumers in Orlan are affected by the tariff. (1 mark)
(e) Explain one reason why a government might impose a tariff. (1 mark)
questions.mark_scheme:
[1] (a) 20% of 200 = 40 dollars.
[1] (b) Working: tariff per bicycle x number imported = 40 x 35,000.
[1] (b) Answer 1,400,000 dollars.
[1] (c) (30,000 - 20,000) / 20,000 x 100 = +50%.
[1] (d) Consumers pay a higher price (240 rather than 200 dollars), so they buy fewer bicycles and have less choice of imports.
[1] (e) A valid reason, e.g. protecting domestic jobs and firms from foreign competition, protecting a new (infant) industry, or raising government revenue.
Accept other valid points.

questions.content:
Yarra is a fast-growing country. The government's main goal is a high rate of economic growth.

Year | GDP (billion dollars) | Forest cover (% of land) | Days per year with dangerous air pollution
2015 | 200 | 38 | 40
2020 | 250 | 31 | 75
2025 | 300 | 25 | 110

(a) Calculate the percentage growth in GDP between 2015 and 2020, and between 2020 and 2025. (2 marks)
(b) Define the term sustainable development. (1 mark)
(c) Analyse whether economic growth in Yarra has been sustainable. Use evidence from the table. (4 marks)
questions.mark_scheme:
[1] (a) 2015 to 2020: (250 - 200) / 200 x 100 = 25%.
[1] (a) 2020 to 2025: (300 - 250) / 250 x 100 = 20%.
[1] (b) Development that meets the needs of people today without harming the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.
[1] (c) Economic benefit with data: GDP rose by 50% from 200 to 300 billion dollars, which can raise incomes and living standards.
[1] (c) Environmental cost: forest cover fell from 38% to 25% of the land (13 percentage points), reducing habitats and natural resources for the future.
[1] (c) Social cost: dangerous pollution days rose from 40 to 110 (2.75 times as many), which harms health and may raise healthcare costs.
[1] (c) Judgement: growth has been rapid but the environmental damage is increasing, so it appears unsustainable unless the government changes policy (e.g. clean energy, forest protection).
Accept other valid points.

questions.content:
Dolvia is a country of 30 million people that exports textiles and fruit. The government is deciding whether to sign a free trade agreement with its large neighbour Marenta. All tariffs between the two countries would be removed over five years.

Current situation (billions of dollars per year)
Dolvian exports to Marenta: 12
Dolvian imports from Marenta: 10
Current average Dolvian tariff on Marentan goods: 15%
Government revenue from these tariffs: 1.5

Forecast after five years under the agreement
Dolvian exports to Marenta: 18
Dolvian imports from Marenta: 17
Prices of imported goods in Dolvia: fall by 12%
Jobs gained in export industries (textiles and fruit): 40,000
Jobs lost in industries that were protected by the tariffs (steel and car assembly): 55,000
Government tariff revenue: 0

Trade balance = value of exports - value of imports.

(a) Calculate Dolvia's trade balance with Marenta now and in the forecast after five years. (2 marks)
(b) Evaluate whether Dolvia should sign the free trade agreement. Use evidence from the information above and reach a justified conclusion. (8 marks)
questions.mark_scheme:
[1] (a) Now: 12 - 10 = +2 billion dollars (surplus).
[1] (a) Forecast: 18 - 17 = +1 billion dollars (surplus).
[1] (b) Export gains with data: exports rise by 50% (12 to 18 billion) and 40,000 jobs are created in textiles and fruit, supporting growth.
[1] (b) Consumer benefit: prices of imports fall by 12%, raising the real income of households and lowering costs for firms that buy imported goods.
[1] (b) Job losses: 55,000 jobs lost against 40,000 gained is a net loss of 15,000 jobs; workers in steel and car assembly may lack skills to move to new jobs (structural unemployment).
[1] (b) Trade balance: the surplus halves from 2 to 1 billion dollars because imports rise faster (70%, from 10 to 17) than exports (50%).
[1] (b) Government finances: 1.5 billion dollars of tariff revenue is lost, reducing funds for public services or for retraining displaced workers.
[1] (b) Evaluative weighing of winners and losers or short run against long run, e.g. consumers and exporters gain while workers in protected industries lose, and long-run gains from specialisation and competition may outweigh short-run adjustment costs.
[1] (b) Recognises uncertainty or a way to reduce harm, e.g. the figures are forecasts, or retraining and phasing in the agreement could help displaced workers.
[1] (b) Clear conclusion consistent with the evidence, with a reasoned justification.
Accept other valid points.
